For Steam Deck owners looking for how to rebind the keys (the default is WASD for movement, which works for most, but sucks for left-handed freaky deaky me), you have to do it via the .ini file.

This is where I found it:

/home/deck/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/495720/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/Local/Intrude/config.ini

You also need to use numerical values for different keys. I use my mouse with my left hand, so I like to rebind from WASD to arrow keys for movement. These are what the values for those are:

straferight="39.000000"
strafeleft="37.000000"
backward="40.000000"
forward="38.000000"

If you want to rebind with something else, you can find other values here (or ask ChatGPT to figure it out for you like I did):

https://www.asciitable.com/

Intrude is a blatant Wolfenstein 3D clone that plays by the motto of ''less is more''.
Its simplicity, visual style and soundtrack are what first got my attention, and I wasn't disappointed... controls are responsive and the gunplay feels great. That's everything I expected! 

Plus, it's a game that rewards strategy. The other side of the coin is that it can get a bit frustrating at times... you need to carefully manage your ammo and health, because there are no resets as you enter the next level, so if you didn't look good in the previous one, you'll probably suffer quite a bit in the next! Also, there is no saving system except the automatic one at the begining of each level, so that's why you have to play it smart.

It's still a Wolf3D clone though, so it is fast-paced, and it even improved on the level design... initially I enjoyed playing Wolfenstein 3D, but after a while the maze-like level design just bored me out of my mind and it took me years to actually beat the whole game (leaving and returning on it every now and then).
Intrude, on the other hand, surely draws influence from that level design, but keeps maps smaller, more straight-forward and quicker to play, thus more enjoyable.

As I hinted, the soundtrack is really good! It almost sounds like a cross between 90s industrial metal, Doom's MIDI soundtrack and Nine Inch Nails (yeah, remember the link between NIN and id Software? I guess these things are all connected, not a coincidence at all). The only complaint I have is I wish it had more tracks (some repeat in various levels)!

It's pretty short, but it's never a downside to me, so take it as you will... it's not an expensive game, after all.
After beating the game the first time you unlock two new modes which honestly just seem like a novelty to me (I don't feel like replaying it anytime soon, even tho I might one day), and the level editor is a great idea to expand the game's life, but having the Steam Workshop implemented would come in VERY handy!

There's also a few minor problems... for instance, it crashed once when I was at the end of a level (instant ragequit for that day), you can't replay selected levels to 100% without replaying the whole thing, and things like that.

Still, if you're into old-school shooters, minimalism and short indie games, I'd say give it a go!

This may be the most simple steam game I've ever yet enjoyed. Aesthetic may give you an impression that because enemies look how they do, this is some bs game but it's really not. It's a wolf3d clone at the core, sure but a really good one. It has both hitscan and projectile enemies. You also get an rocketlauncher.

Definite minus is that it has no automap as I know that can be a problem for some players. Sound effects are very good for what this is, not some pew pew bangs. Music also includes some quite rocking tunes.

The controls are simple and quite responsive. However sometimes when firing pistol in quick succession, the mouse will not register all clicks. Framerate is also capped at 60fps but you can run higher refreshrates. Other than that, I'd recommend this if you know what you're getting into. Small little throwback fps for the afternoon.

Intrude is a small project that tried to capture the likes of Wolfenstein 3D with a few modern ammenties and graphic improvements. Although much shorter, it is still a fun experience as it has 3 episodes of 5 levels for each. I know mentioning Wolf 3D might turn people off as it can be very difficult to navigate, but with the level layouts being somewhat smaller sometimes and varied textures, it is easier to find your way.

You get 5 weapons, a knife which is a one-shot for most enemies, a pistol which is good for the whole game, a shotgun which is better up close, a machine gun which shoots faster with less accuracy, and a rocket launcher that does a ton of damage. Each with their own ammo and done well enough in this game that they are fine to use and have a purpose for each throughout. The music is nice, just wish there was more than 5 tracks.

The enemies are different colored, but unnamed soldiers, each with a different weapon from your arsenal. Greens have a pistol, Browns have a baton, Purples have a machine gun, Blues have a rocket launcher, and there is a moving sentry and the final boss. Somewhat simple to fight, but they work and for some reason have telepathy as they often shoot before your round a corner and can never be ambushed. Which brings me to the only bug I found. The Purples shoot a burst and it seems there is something wrong with the targeting because I have had them hit me through walls. Besides that, my only complaint is there desperately needs to be map and stat counter if you want to 100% and helps navigate. There are guides for both already, just kind of needs to be in the game, but the dev(s) seem to have left this project.

In conclusion, a fun experience if you are wanting to play something like Wolf 3D, but shorter and easier.

Intrude is really bland and kinda boring, and is missing some essential components even games made 20 years ago had. 

It's a Wolfenstein 3D clone, meaning all the levels exist on a flat plane and you also can't look up or down. Although it's a clone of that game, it doesn't have quick-saving or a map which makes navigating its maze-like levels tedious. The levels themselves are not as complex as your average Wolf3D level but they're still big enough to get lost in and the visual design of the levels is not as good, everything looks the same with the same wall textures and floors.

It's not the worst thing ever, but I just see no reason to play this when many games have done this formula better. Even if you've played Wolfenstein 3D already and want something similar, this really isn't worth your time.

While the lack of quick saves is not for everyone and there are some cruel level design moments, it's still genuinely challenging for the most part.

+ Decent enemy variety.
+ Decent weapon variety.
+ Weapons have good impact.
+ Good aesthetics and graphics.

[h1]Negatives[/h1]

This is a game that's clearly designed to imitate the classicest of classic shooters, 1992's Wolfenstein 3D, and it does a pretty good job except for some SERIOUS frustrations.

Pros:
-Art style is suitably old-school
-Enemies are clearly distinct
-Weapons feel good to use (other than the shotgun reload taking too long)
-Music is good

Cons:
-Game is very short (15 levels total - maybe 2 hours of content)
-Levels are rather mazey and there's no map (not a big deal given the inspiration)
-The game randomly hard-freezes, requiring a Windows+Tab to switch to a new desktop so you can open task manager and kill the process
-Enemies can kind of shoot you through corners, so you're getting hit by enemies you can't even see.
-NO SAVE FUNCTION. Being able to save mid-level has been around for 30 years now. For crying out loud, the 30-year-old-game this is aping even has mid-level-saving. So, if there's a tough spot on a level and you die (say running down a hallway facing 30 robot enemies that can shoot you before you can really see them), replay the entire level up to that point to try again. Oh, you died again? Then try again again. Oops, the game froze on this attempt? Try again again again. Some of the levels are around 10 minutes long, too, so hooray wasted time.

I really want to like this game more than I do. I bought it at full price during a sale (heresy, I know) because it looked right up my alley, but I just can't recommend it without some MAJOR caveats. If they were to add in a save function, this would be an undeniable recommendation, but it's very frustrating having to replay entire levels over and over and over and over due to some weird design choice that hasn't ever been a part of even the original games in this genre. If you love old-school nostalgia shooters, it might be worth taking a look, but you might find yourself frustrated too. I wish there were a middle-thumb rating, honestly.

Узнал об этой игре благодаря обзору Newbilius (Old-Hard.ru).

В общем, Intrude - это клон Wolfenstein3D и Corridor7 от фаната для фанатов.
Сюжет не имеет особо значения, он лишь задаёт сеттинг происходящего, а именно - военная база будущего с лазерами и супер компьютерами.
Вы сбегаете из тюрьмы, охрана вас пытается сначала отдубасить дубинками, затем попытается застрелить из дробовиков, потом из автоматов, а потом из ракетниц. И вот я перечислил почти все типы врагов. Ваш арсенал, следовательно, пополняется аналогичными пушками, со временем.

Подход разработчика к картостроению вполне здравый (но не без огрехов) - сначала вам демонстративно показывают нововведение (лазерная ловушка, разрушаемые стены и т.д.), а уже потом отправляют вглубь карты, где фишки применяются на деле. То есть в игре нет ситуаций, когда вы не знаете, что делает та или иная вещь. Плюс, фишки наслаиваются постепенно, вам, как минимум, дают пройти целый уровень, чтобы свыкнуться с механиками.

Однако, игра не слишком легкая. Даже на обычной (она тут минимальная) сложности патронов пусть и хватает, но впритык. Та же история с броней и аптечками. А количество врагов растёт с каждым новым уровнем. Уровней всего 15, тематически они разделены на 3 эпизода. На три эпизода всего три трека. [b]KURZ-REVIEW:[/b]
[h1]Minimalistischer Wolfenstein-3D-Klon mit Anspruch[/h1]

Wenn ein Spiel die Bezeichnung »[i][b]Wolfenstein 3D[/b][/i]-Klon« verdient hat, dann das mit dem GameMaker Studio entwickelte [i][b]Intrude[/b][/i]. In diesem sollen wir mit unserem namenlosen Protagonisten eine eigentlich längst stillgelegte Untergrund-Basis infiltrieren, in der sich unbekannte, paramilitärische Einheiten eingenistet haben. Das Ziel: Ebene 15.

Auf dem Weg dahin schießen wir uns mit einem recht konventionellen und überschaubaren Arsenal (Pistole, Pumpaction, Minigun und Raketenwerfer) durch Soldaten mit derselbigen Bewaffnung. Das Environment ist wie in [i][b]Wolfenstein 3D[/b][/i] sehr schlicht gehalten, jeder der 15 Level sieht abgesehen vom Level-Layout identisch aus, Vertikalität gibt es nicht. Der ein oder andere hält dann aber doch auch eine Überraschung parat. Die Spielzeit ist vergleichsweise kurz – es gibt sogar ein Achievement dafür, das Spiel in unter einer Stunde durchzuspielen.

Das dürfte im ersten Durchgang aber eher nicht zu schaffen sein; [i][b]Intrude[/b][/i] bietet durchaus den Anreiz für mehrere Partien. Zu Beginn ist nur der Standard-Modus verfügbar, nach einmaligem Durchspielen können wir entweder im »Melter«- oder »Explosive«-Modus von vorne beginnen. In ersterem verschießen alle Waffen (also auch die der Gegner) Energiebolzen, die mehr Schaden verursachen. In letzterem ... nun, das kann man sich denken. Tatsächlich ist der Retro-Shooter kein Titel, in dem man einfach wie ein T-850 durch die Gänge marschieren und wild um sich ballern sollte. Gerade die späteren Level sind recht knackig – mit Healtpoints aber auch mit Munition sollte, trotz überall verteilten Medpacks und Muni-Kisten, nicht allzu sorglos umgegangen werden – sonst steht man plötzlich auf Ebene 12 nur noch mit dem Messer und 8 HP da. Zusätzlich erschwert wird das Ganze dadurch, dass nur am jeweiligen Level-Anfang gespeichert wird – freies Speichern gibt’s nicht.

Als weiteren Ausgleich für den überschaubaren Umfang hat [i][b]Intrude[/b][/i] einen der wohl am einfachsten zu bedienenden Level-Editoren mit an Bord, denn die Videospielgeschichte je gesehen hat. Damit könnte selbst eine Amöbe etwas vernünftig hinbekommen. Schade ist jedoch, dass der grundsätzlich gelungene Soundtrack nur recht wenige Stücke zu bieten hat.

[b][u]FAZIT[/u][/b]
[i][b]Intrude[/b][/i] ist in fast jeder Hinsicht, wie sein großes Vorbild nach heutigem Maßstab, recht minimalistisch gehalten. Dafür ist es aber kein Spaziergang im Park. Zwar ist der erste Playthrough schnell erledigt, [i][b]Intrude[/b][/i] kann aber durchaus durch die freischaltbaren Modi zum mehrmaligen Durchspielen motivieren. Für die 4 Euro Standard-Preis für Leute mit einem entsprechenden Faible für derartige Retro-Shooter definitiv einen Blick wert, mit einem ähnlich gelagerten [i][b]Project Warlock[/b][/i] kann es aber eindeutig nicht mithalten.

Intrude is an oldschool Wolfenstein/Doom hybrid. While enjoyable and short, it is plagued with a few frustrating design choices.

The graphics are pixelated and the art style is, as mentioned, a well-done mix of Wolfenstein and DOOM. The music is absolutely amazing, and it's a shame there is only one track per episode, a little variety would've gone a long way.

And that's kind of a recurring theme here. There are is a knife and four weapons (pistol, shotgun, minigun, rocket launcher) which all use their respective ammo type (bullets, shells, large bullets and rockets). Basic, but effective. There are four human enemies which are all pixelated dudes of various colors: white - melee attack, green - pistol attack, purple - assault rifle, blue - rocket launcher. Then there's the classic 90s annoying enemy type, a small drone with a rather infuriatingly small hitbox. Again, there isn't much, but what there is... it's good. Would it be better if there were more enemy types and guns? Yes. Are the ones present enough? Sure.

But it all boils down to the most important question: is the game fun and worth your money? There are two answers here. If you're fed up playing Wolf3D/Spear of Destiny or DOOM for the n+1th time or you're after a short but quality distraction, definitely. It plays more or less the same as these games and the game consists of 15 levels broken up into three episodes (5 levels) each and they feature the standard key-hunting and pixel-dude exterminating gameplay of yore. It worked then, and it works now. I wished it were a bit longer (then again, I don't - see below) health and ammo were just a teensy bit more generously distributed, but if you're careful and don't waste resources, you should be fine. In short, the game is good, the controls are responsive, the enemy AI is excellent considering the budget this game was made with, they have recognizable attack patterns (I wish they would have unique callouts, instead they all just shout the same "Hey!"), they retreat and flank you... Good stuff. The weapons are also few, but, again, effective. To sum up, it ticks all the boxes in the gameplay department (maybe not the "extremely complex shooting" one).

EDIT: I just finished the game twice in "Melting" mode (going for the speedrun achievement) which transforms your bullets into cell projectiles - but also the enemies' fire! This game is what the base game should have been. Projectile-based gameplay is so much more rewarding and intense than hitscan (not saying hitscan is bad, but I strongly prefer projectile). "Explosive" mode is ridiculous though, but I think that was kind of the point.

I said there are two answers to "is the game fun?", so here's the second one. This game is fun, yes, but if you're a completionist... stay away from this game. FAR away. It's not worth it. Why? Because there's no saving in this game apart from the auto-save at the beginning of your last played level. Let me rephrase that: in order to get the achievements to find all the secrets/kills/barrels/data cores in the game, you have to do so in ONE playthrough in the ONLY slot this game provides you with. The game doesn't even have a real-time tally of collected secrets and killed enemies, so you can't know if you've missed something until you've FINISHED the level. Missed a barrel on level 13 of 15? Tough, you have to restart the whole game. Missed one enemy in level 3? Start over. This is downright infuriating and honestly, it's a totally cheap way to waste your time. I really can't decide which tactic would waste more time: try and get all the collectibles in one playthrough or focus on one collectible in multiple playthroughs. I think the creator of this game thought to himself "how could squeeze the most playtime from people in this 2-something-hour game?" or something, because it's baffling to me. While I agree that quicksaves can be abused and these games can become too easy if that happens, the very LEAST that could be implemented was a hud element that shows "Data cores: 0/1, Kills: 45/64 etc." to let the player know they're not done - it would still lengthen the playtime and I'd actually WANT to explore the well-designed levels instead of fearing the Exit button. Or, you could give the player a choice when they hit the exit button: LMB - next level, R - restart level. There are numerous other ways to squeeze extra hours from players, but the way it was done in this game is seriously the worst way I've ever seen. I hate checkpoint systems, but I'd take that over this crap anyday. Yeah, an argument could be made that the levels aren't long, but that's a bad excuse for a cheap way to increase difficulty and total playtime. Put another way, this game wants to make you NOT want to play it. I'm a completionist, sometimes even when it's not worth it, and a stubborn person to boot - if you can get *me* to throw my hands in the air and say "not worth it", then you done messed up somewhere. EDIT: someone was kind enough to post maps with collectible locations, and that makes the whole thing a lot more doable and bearable, but it's still an annoying mechanic.

Other than a lack of saving, there are some oddly basic things missing from the game. There's no sprint feature (I hope I don't have to tell you that you can't jump, crouch or look up/down), although I didn't really feel there was need for one other than pandering to people like me who are used to it. However, there is no option for custom keybindings altogether (if you don't have a QWERTY/QWERTZ keyboard, good luck), no windowed mode, the Steam overlay works but screenshots don't. At least there's a FOV slider and a mouse sensitivity setting, but apart from the resolution (all 16:9) that's pretty much it.

Some people will say "yeah, but the game was made by one person", and I agree it's an amazing game for a one-man project (well, two-man if you count the guy who did the music), but that doesn't automatically absolve you of any criticism for lacking basic features games have had since 1991. I mean, no custom keybinds... seriously?

So at the end, should you buy it? I'd say yes, it's cheap as it is and it's like 2€ during sales, but be aware what you're in for: great gameplay, artstyle and music, but a severe lack of features and a frustrating save system (or lack thereof).

"Intrude" is a neat little game that will keep you entertained for quite a few hours: the main levels are not that many, but after finishing the game for the first time you unlock two new modes, while always having access to also a nice set of custom levels, which increases a lot the game replayability. I am by no means an expert in this type of game as I usually prefer much different titles, but I had a lot of fun with this one and the satisfaction I got from finishing it was immense. Well worth the 4€, and now it's even on sale so just get it!

I got this game for just over a dollar (in my Indian currency on Steam) during a discount, and have to say I enjoyed it. The game's around about 3 hours in length, and takes all the inspiration from Wolfenstein 3d. 

For anyone who's never played Wolf 3d, I don't know if they could enjoy it unless they like some maze like levels that could occasionally get them lost. This is a nostalgia throwback, and gotta be honest, for the little it has, it entertained me. It's a SIMPLE game in its approach, but may appear complicated to anyone who is used to modern day features like minimap etc, which in my personal opinion almost always has been a reason for the decline in  level design in gaming. 

It's not nearly as good as Doom's level design though. Doom always gave you recognizable areas but here everything looks alike. So while that could be a turn off for many, it's not trying to be Doom, it's trying to be Wolfenstein 3d, and for a cheap indie game, it suceeds at that. I think it's still easy enough to memorize the level layouts and finish the game in 3 hours.
